channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Zema: Tornar vacinação obrigatória não é o que pode acontecer num país democrático
item.description: Romeu Zema, candidate from the New Party for the Presidency, stated he is against mandatory vaccination, deeming it undemocratic, during an interview with Jornal Nacional. Despite being fully vaccinated himself, he advocates for individual freedom.

item.title: Zema já admite manter valorização do mínimo e quer esperar para alterar idade para aposentar
item.description: In a TV Globo interview, Romeu Zema (Novo) admitted he might keep the minimum wage increase and hesitated on raising the retirement age, signaling flexibility in his fiscal adjustment plan. He also avoided taking a firm stance on structural reforms, opting to wait for more economic context.

item.title: Zema, sobre salário mínimo: Garanto que ninguém vai ter perda; se tiver inflação, nós daremos
item.description: Romeu Zema, candidate of the Novo party for the Presidency, stated that he will ensure inflation-adjusted minimum wage increases, without harm to workers, if elected. In an interview with Jornal Nacional, he reiterated there will be no loss in the minimum wage and any inflation impact will be offset.

item.title: Quaest: veja como está a disputa entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro em AL, MA, PR, RN, RS e SC
item.description: Quaest released polling data for the presidential race in six Brazilian states (AL, MA, PR, RN, RS, SC), showing the contest between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro. Results vary by region, reflecting distinct voter profiles. Coverage focuses solely on vote intentions, without platform analysis.

item.title: Flávio: Vou montar um time de ministros competentes, como a Daniella Marques que está aqui
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, PL candidate for President of Brazil, announced his intention to form a team of competent ministers if elected, citing former Caixa Econômica Federal president Daniella Marques as an example. He emphasized the importance of having qualified professionals in the government team.

item.title: Pesquisa indica a dificuldade duradoura na campanha eleitoral de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign faces challenges with female voters, according to BTG Pactual/Nexus research. Lula leads among women with 48% voting intentions against Flávio's 31%, while the scenario reverses among men. The issue is linked to Jair Bolsonaro's image and Michelle Bolsonaro's absence from events.

item.title: Zema não garante aumento real do salário mínimo e diz que, 'por ora', não mexeria em idades de aposentadoria
item.description: Romeu Zema stated that if elected, he will only ensure inflation adjustment for the minimum wage without committing to real increases, and has no immediate plans to change retirement ages, tying future reforms to economic performance and labor market formalization.

item.title: Quem são os candidatos ao Senado por Goiás (GO) nas eleições 2026
item.description: In the 2026 elections, Goiás will elect two new federal senators, with ELEVEN confirmed pre-candidates. Key names include Vanderlan Cardoso (PSD), seeking re-election, and Gracinha Caiado (União), former first lady of the state. The race will be decided in a single round on October 4th, for seats previously held by Jorge Kajuru and Vanderlan Cardoso.

item.title: Quaest: em SC, Flávio Bolsonaro tem 45% e Lula 20% no 1º turno
item.description: A Quaest poll in Santa Catarina shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading with 45% against Lula (PT) at 20% in the first round of 2026. Pablo Marçal (PRTB) does not significantly change the scenario, holding 2% of voting intention. The margin of error is 3 points, with 13% undecided and 8% blank/null votes.

item.title: Erika Hilton “desafia” Flávio a debater fim da escala 6 X 1
item.description: Federal deputy Erika Hilton (Psol-SP) challenged senator and presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro to a public debate on the PEC proposing the end of the 6 X 1 work schedule, following a O Globo report accusing Flávio of mobilizing Senate allies to delay the vote. The PEC, filed by Erika in 2024, has government support and divides opinion in the opposition. The vote is scheduled for September 2nd at the Senate CCJ.

item.title: No JN, Zema comete gafe e diz que tem “série de programas contra mulheres”
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) made a gaffe during a Jornal Nacional interview by saying he has 'a series of programs against women,' when referring to measures to combat violence against women. The statement was widely criticized on social media as a major misstep, though Zema later clarified that the initiatives include expanding specialized police stations, creating shelters for domestic violence victims, and using electronic ankle bracelets for offenders. He also advocated for awareness programs in schools and was questioned about Minas Gerais' public debt, which he attributed to inherited liabilities from previous administrations.

item.title: Em "Dark Horse" e Lulinha, Justiça não é cega; enxerga com um olho só
item.description: The text criticizes the perception of partiality in the Brazilian justice system, suggesting that investigations against political figures such as Lula and those involved in the 'Dark Horse' case are influenced by electoral motives. It questions the impartiality of ministers and media pressure on judicial decisions, advocating for greater transparency in investigations.

item.title: PF investiga operador financeiro de amiga de Lulinha para saques e pagamentos em dinheiro vivo
item.description: Federal Police investigate financial operator Ulisses Barbosa, accused of facilitating cash withdrawals and payments for lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, possibly covering flights of President Lula's son. The investigation raises money laundering suspicions and highlights the use of travel accounts to conceal expenses, with Roberta also probed for influence peddling.

item.title: Veja o que é #FATO e o que é #FAKE na entrevista de Romeu Zema à Globo
item.description: Romeu Zema was the first presidential candidate interviewed by Globo in a series of debates with candidates for the presidency. In the interview, he highlighted the fiscal recovery of Minas Gerais, claiming he took office with a deficit of BRL 11 billion and left with a surplus of BRL 5 billion. The Fact Check team analyzed his statements, verifying the state government's budget data.

item.title: Zema na TV Globo: como o ex-governador se saiu na entrevista? Veja as notas e avaliações dos colunistas do GLOBO
item.description: In his interview with TV Globo, Romeu Zema was criticized for his hesitant and simplistic performance, receiving low scores from columnists. The former governor defended positions close to Bolsonarismo but faced questions about failures in his management in Minas Gerais. The series of debates continues with other presidential candidates.

item.title: Ministro do Brasil e representante do governo Lula aceram reunião na próxima segunda-feira para discutir tarifaço
item.description: The Brazilian Minister of Development, Márcio Elias Rosa, and the U.S. Trade Representative, Jamieson Greer, scheduled a virtual meeting to resume negotiations on tariffs imposed on Brazilian exports. The dialogue was rekindled after a phone call between Presidents Lula and Trump, focusing on potential exemptions from the 25% and 12.5% tariffs.

item.title: O que diz Simone Tebet, na chapa de Haddad, sobre caso Lulinha
item.description: Simone Tebet, PSB candidate for the Senate, stated in an interview with VEJA that suspicions involving President Lula’s son, Fábio Luis, must be investigated swiftly, autonomously, and without double standards. She emphasized equal treatment for all cases, referencing parallel investigations such as that of Flávio Bolsonaro. She denied that her candidacy would be affected by her alliance with Lula, highlighting her independent political trajectory.

item.title: Flávio se esquiva de “Dark Horse” e cobra “follow the money” de Lulinha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro avoided commenting on the accounting of 'Dark Horse' and attacked Fábio Lulinha, son of Lula, demanding transparency about expenses in Spain. During an event at Fiesp, he claimed responsibility is not his and questioned funding for Lulinha. The STF authorized sharing data from the investigation into the film's production company.

item.title: Flávio nega acordo com Tarcísio sobre reeleição
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) denied negotiating with Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) regarding the end of presidential re-election as a condition for greater involvement in the campaign. The statement was made in São Paulo after a meeting with business representatives.

item.title: Zema defende “modelo Bukele” e critica Judiciário “caro e lerdo”
item.description: Presidential candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) said he intends to adopt security measures inspired by Nayib Bukele's model in El Salvador and criticized the judiciary as 'expensive and slow'. In an interview with TV Globo, he argued that 'the place for a criminal is behind bars' and positioned himself as the only candidate with his own proposals for public security.

item.title: Skaf diz que Flávio defende valores da Fiesp, mas evita declarar apoio
item.description: Paulo Skaf, president of Fiesp, praised Flávio Bolsonaro's proposals but avoided declaring formal support, highlighting ideological convergence. During a São Paulo meeting, Flávio advocated for reduced business costs, stronger legal security and technical autonomy in ministries. Skaf emphasized the need to protect Brazilian industry from unfair foreign competition.

item.title: Lula x Flávio: pesquisas mostram como está a disputa presidencial nos estados da região Sul
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro leads in Southern region polls with significant advantages over Lula, especially in Santa Catarina. In all three states, the PL candidate maintains strong voter intentions while Lula struggles to attract voters.

item.title: Lobista amiga de Lulinha recebeu 300 mil em espécie e seria 'costumeiro' pagar passagens de filho do presidente, aponta PF
item.description: The Brazilian Federal Police are investigating President Lula's son, Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger over alleged influence peddling. A report claims Roberta received R$300,000 in cash and paid for Lulinha’s flights. The defendants deny wrongdoing, and their lawyers claim the leaks aim to sway the 2026 election.

item.title: Zema atribui dívida mineira a juros cobrados pela União
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo), a pre-candidate for the presidency, stated in a debate that Minas Gerais' debt to the federal government stems from high interest rates charged by the central government, not new loans during his state tenure.

item.title: VÍDEOS: Tralli e Renata entrevistam Romeu Zema, candidato a presidente pelo Novo
item.description: Romeu Zema, running for president under the Novo party, was interviewed by Tralli and Renata on topics including public debt, privatizations, minimum wage, pension reform, and mining frauds in Minas Gerais. In further remarks, Zema does not promise a real increase in the minimum wage and states that, for now, he would not change retirement ages. The 2026 elections remain dominated by figures such as Flávio Dix, Lula, and Moro in the polls.

item.title: Zema promete anistia a Bolsonaro e aponta “julgamento político”
item.description: Presidential candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) promised a pardon to former president Jair Bolsonaro (PL) if elected, describing the January 2023 coup attempt as an act of vandalism and suggesting a possible political trial against Bolsonaro.

item.title: A eleição de 2026 parece ser a pior desde a redemocratização
item.description: The 2026 presidential debate reflects a disheartened election, with Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro dominating without room for a competitive center, while figures like Ronaldo Caiado remain marginalized. The campaign is marked by criticism of the lack of innovative proposals and polarization between the two leaders, who, according to Caiado, 'have nothing to show but much to hide'.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro nega que pediu engajamento de Tarcísio na campanha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro denied asking Tarcísio for more campaign engagement, stating they have a good relationship and always work together even without a formal pact. During an event at Fiesp, he also commented on the Dark Horse movie, criticizing questions about the biography of his father, Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Antes de Nikolas, Ana Castela já precisou se explicar por “22” em show
item.description: Ana Castela faced a similar controversy in 2022, when a video shown during her show linked the number 22 to the PL and Jair Bolsonaro. She denied political involvement and distanced herself from the message. This incident foreshadowed her recent 2026 image with Nikolas Ferreira, also tied to the PL.

item.title: Zema na TV Globo: candidato minimiza situação fiscal de MG, ataca o governo federal e critica STF por condenações do 8/1
item.description: In an interview with TV Globo, Romeu Zema defended his management in Minas Gerais, downplayed state debt, and criticized interest rates charged by the federal government. He also attacked the STF over convictions related to the January 8th events, promised amnesty, and advocated for privatizations and a stricter justice system.

item.title: US Open: Thiago Wild avança no quali; 4 brasileiros são eliminados
item.description: Thiago Wild, the Brazilian tennis player ranked 202 in the ATP rankings, was the only Brazilian to advance in the US Open qualifiers, defeating Italian Raul Brancaccio 2-0. Gustavo Heide, Felipe Meligeni, Laura Pigossi, and Luísa Stefani were eliminated in the qualifying rounds. Wild's next match will be against Mackenzie McDonald on Wednesday (August 26) at 11 AM.

item.title: Visita ao Poder360: Eduardo Girão
item.description: Senator Eduardo Girão, running mate for Romeu Zema, visited Poder360 and criticized PL's support for Ciro Gomes, defending amnesty for Jair Bolsonaro while discussing privatizations, abortion, and political polarization.

item.title: Como está a disputa pela Presidência em 6 estados, segundo a Quaest
item.description: The Quaest institute updated the presidential poll intentions in six Brazilian states. Flávio Bolsonaro leads in Paraná (41%) and Santa Catarina (45%), while Lula is ahead in Rio Grande do Sul (28%) and Rio Grande do Norte (56%). Surveys were conducted between August 20 and 23 with a margin of error of three percentage points.

item.title: Ancine concede registro a 'Dark Horse', cinebiografia de Jair Bolsonaro
item.description: Ancine granted the Foreign Work Registry to 'Dark Horse', a biographical film about Jair Bolsonaro, which is under judicial investigation for suspected funding irregularities and unauthorized filming in Brazil.

item.title: Flávio promete ‘tesouraço’ na política fiscal e critica juros da dívida pública
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), presidential candidate, promised a spending 'axe' in public finances, criticizing President Lula's fiscal policy for prioritizing tax collection over spending cuts. He proposed tax cuts, anti-corruption measures, bureaucratic streamlining, and the creation of a sovereign data center with AI to track public funds. The senator also highlighted the high cost of public debt interest, reaching R$ 4 billion per day, criticizing the allocation of these resources.

item.title: Emenda parlamentares são o 'maior vetor de corrupção' da burocracia estatal, diz Flávio Dino
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino labeled parliamentary amendments as the biggest vector of corruption in the public bureaucracy during an event at USP’s Money Laundering Study Group. He cited examples such as ghost works, overpriced purchases, and questionable medical procedures funded by these amendments. Dino also pointed to the pandemic as the starting point for the misuse of the Secret Budget.

item.title: Zema propõe ajuste fiscal para baixar juros a 6%, sem detalhar medidas, e defende anistia para condenados do 8 de janeiro
item.description: Zema, Novo's presidential candidate, proposed cutting the Selic rate from 14% to 6% annually through fiscal adjustment, without specifying the measures. He pledged minimum wage increases tied to inflation and supported amnesty for January 8 convicts, focusing on credibility and anti-corruption efforts without detailing privatizations.

item.title: Paulo Skaf diz que Flávio Bolsonaro defende valores que Fiesp acredita
item.description: Paulo Skaf, president of Fiesp, stated that Flávio Bolsonaro advocates for economic values shared by the entity, expressing sympathy without formally endorsing his presidential bid.

item.title: Flávio propõe pontuação para pobres que querem “melhorar de vida”
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro proposed a scoring system for low-income individuals who take actions such as completing primary school, vaccinating children, and enrolling in daycare, inspired by credit cards. The initiative is part of the Ganha-Ganha program, offering technical courses and microcredit to reduce dependency on aids like Bolsa Família. He emphasized maintaining the benefit, but stressed it should be the beginning, not the end, of state intervention.

item.title: Flávio promete “ministros técnicos” e diz que “resolverá no Congresso”
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro pledged, during a meeting with FIESP, to form a government with technical ministers and personally handle congressional negotiations to pass priority bills, especially in the economy. He highlighted his 24-year legislative experience as a key asset of his campaign and announced new names for the economic team. The strategy reinforces the focus on technical freedom and autonomy in government portfolios.

item.title: Título de eleitor e biometria regular: veja como fazer a consulta pela internet
item.description: Voters can check online the status of their voter ID and verify if their biometric data is registered through the TSE's online service or the e-Título app. The free service shows whether the registration is regular, suspended, or canceled, and confirms the biometric status.

item.title: 'Quem tem que prestar contas não sou eu', diz Flávio Bolsonaro sobre filme Dark Horse
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro denied backtracking on accountability for the film 'Dark Horse', claiming the producer had already disclosed expenses in the investigation. He shifted responsibility to the Lula government, accusing it of secret meetings with businessmen. The STF authorized PF access to data from the operation against the film's producer.

item.title: ‘Vocês vão parar no tempo?’, reclama Flávio ao ser cobrado por prestação de contas do Dark Horse
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro dismissed demands for accountability regarding the Dark Horse film, claiming he's not responsible and accusing the press of trying to link him to the Banco Master case. He stated the production company already submitted a report during an investigation in São Paulo and downplayed the need for further transparency, while warning about press freedom under a PT government.

item.title: Quaest em SC: Flávio Bolsonaro, 45%; Lula, 20%; Renan Santos, 4%
item.description: Quaest poll for SC shows Flávio Bolsonaro leading with 45%, ahead of Lula with 20% in the presidential race. Pablo Marçal appears with 2% in the broader scenario. 70% of voters claim to have made their decision.

item.title: Flávio, sobre caso Dark Horse: Vocês estão parados no tempo?
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL presidential candidate, reacted to questions about the Dark Horse case by asking if journalists are 'stuck in time'. He denied responsibility for explaining the film's financial records.

item.title: Skaf insinua apoio a Flávio após evento com candidato na Fiesp
item.description: Paulo Skaf, president of Fiesp, stated he will support the presidential candidate who defends the entity's principles after an event with Flávio Bolsonaro, while emphasizing Fiesp's non-partisan stance. Skaf criticized protectionist policies and advocated for reducing state interference in society.

item.title: Veja como foi a segunda-feira (24) dos candidatos a presidente
item.description: On Monday (24), the presidential candidates carried out campaign agendas featuring debates, interviews, and sectoral events. Topics covered included economy, health, education, and security, with emphasis on proposals to combat job insecurity and privatization. Candidates also engaged in media training and communication activities.

item.title: Haddad para empresários: "O Brasil está bem endereçado"
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) stated that Brazil is 'well-positioned' during a dinner with infrastructure business leaders in São Paulo, advocating for reforms and criticizing the fiscal management of Tarcísio de Freitas. Haddad highlighted the decline in GDP and state investment, and pledged to review Sabesp and rail transport concession contracts if elected.

item.title: CCJ do Senado deve votar a PEC da 6 X 1 em 2 de setembro, diz Randolfe
item.description: The PEC ending the 6 X 1 work scale is expected to be voted on at the Senate CCJ on September 2nd, according to the Government leader in Congress, Randolfe Rodrigues. The proposal, under the rapporteurship of Omar Aziz, follows a public hearing on August 26th and proceeds with accelerated processing before the 2026 elections.

item.title: Justiça Eleitoral manda retirar “Fora Lula” de ônibus de Salles
item.description: São Paulo Electoral Court ordered Senate candidate Ricardo Salles to remove 'Fora Lula' stickers and a depiction of Pixuleco from his bus, under a daily fine of R$3,000. The ruling was issued by judge Claudia Fanucchi, partially upholding a PT lawsuit and requiring compliance within 24 hours while allowing the bus to remain in circulation. The campaign faced criticism for featuring offensive content targeting President Lula.
